routes.label: enrolment and collection at an ANRPTS centre

note: The Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada's response (August 2015), quoting the decree that brought the card into force: it is valid ten years and compulsory for every Mauritanian of 16 enrolled in the National Population Biometric Register. Its sources gave the fee as 1,000 ouguiya in 2012-2013; the ouguiya has been redenominated since, and no fee in today's currency was found, so it's null. The time isn't stated.

sources.title: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada, Mauritania: National identity documents in use (2012-July 2015), on ecoi.net
sources.said: The Decree stipulates that the identity card is valid for ten years and [translation] “is mandatory for all Mauritanians who are at least sixteen (16) years of age and enrolled in the National Population Biometric Register ... a fee of 1,000 ouguiya [approximately C$5] must be paid in order to obtain the identity card
